properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), limitation 9: no loop nudge reaches a VS Code agent on the --call door, for three stacked reasons. (1) init and the server count only Claude Code and OpenCode as trigger harnesses, so a VS Code project gets no hook. (2) The nudge script counts writes by MCP tool name only (`reflow2` and `__` in tool_name), so a terminal --call write is never counted even where the script runs. (3) loop_status tells a VS Code project "none is possible", which VS Code's hooks now contradict
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent D, on limitation 9 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("No loop nudges. Nothing prompts loop_status at a boundary in VS Code.").

① OBSERVED (reported): nothing prompts loop_status at a session boundary. EXPECTED: what Claude Code gets. tools/loop_nudge.py runs on SessionStart (orientation text), PostToolUse (counts writes) and Stop (blocks once with "N graph write(s) this session and no loop check"). reflow2_init.py's ensure_hooks writes it into .claude/settings.local.json, and reflow2_install.py into ~/.claude/settings.json. NOT AFFECTED: an agent can still call loop_status itself.

② PRECEDENT: dec:idea-the-loop-nudge-exists-for-one-harness-only chose "announce the absence" and kept "ship a per-harness equivalent where an event model is confirmed". req:an-unavailable-loop-trigger-is-named-as-unavailable is the announcement.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) VS Code has no hook model; (b) it has one, and reflow2 installs nothing for it; (c) even with hooks running, the nudge cannot see --call writes; (d) the agent never reads the announcement.

⑤ MEASURED (origin/main 66620f7, 0.77.0):
- (a) REFUTED by VS Code's docs: fact:vs-code-has-an-agent-hook-event-model-reflow2-can-register-against-2026-10-02.
- (b) HOLDS. reflow2_init.py has HOOK_HARNESS = "claude" and the server has TRIGGER_HARNESSES = ["claude", "opencode"] (nudge.rs). Running main's init with `--harness vscode` on a scratch project printed "loop nudge NOT INSTALLED — reflow2 has no hook for vscode; only Claude Code has an event model it can register against" and wrote no hook file (log: triage-D/l11-init-vscode.log).
- (c) HOLDS, and is the deeper cause. main's loop_nudge.py was fed hook events in a scratch project (log: triage-D/l9-nudge.log):
  - a Claude-shaped PostToolUse (tool_name mcp__reflow2__add_requirement) then Stop gave the block decision;
  - a terminal-shaped PostToolUse (tool_name run_in_terminal, tool_input.command "reflow2-mcp ... --call add_requirement ...") then Stop gave nothing, and no state file was written.
  The counter keys on `"reflow2" in tool and "__" in tool`. So VS Code running the existing hook (chat.useClaudeHooks) would still never nudge after a door write.
- (d) PARTLY. loop_status on a vscode-stamped scratch project returns nudge = no_hook_for_this_harness, with the advisory "THERE IS NO SESSION-END NUDGE FOR THIS HARNESS, and none is possible ... reflow2 has a trigger only for Claude Code (a Stop hook) and OpenCode (a plugin)". The advisory does reach a door agent, because it rides loop_status's reply. Its "none is possible" is stale for VS Code.

⑥ CLASS: the nudge's notion of "a write" is the MCP tool name, so any route that writes without an MCP tool call is invisible to it. The --call door is one. The same blindness would cover `--import`. A VS Code port must count door writes some other way: parse the executable position and the `--call <tool>` argument of the command (not words in it; see limitation 20), or have the door itself leave a per-session marker. Would the fix have stopped other occurrences? It would also cover any non-MCP route that writes.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: VS Code's terminal tool name and tool_input shape (run_in_terminal was a stand-in; any non-MCP name gives the same result); whether the reporter's organisation allows hooks.
